source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
OCB1 publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 120,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, the same power supports roughly 900 racks. The arithmetic is straightforward, but the right figure depends entirely on what load is deployed, and the operator does not publish a rack count or density target.

The six certifications qualify the campus to host payment card data under PCI DSS, protected health information under HIPAA and HITRUST, federal information systems under FISMA, and general enterprise workloads audited to SSAE 18 and TIA-942 standards. Those credentials point toward regulated-industry tenants rather than hyperscale AI training, which tends to prefer raw scale over compliance overhead. Whether any AI workload runs here is not published.

Iowa has 52 mapped facilities, but only 2 of them publish a megawatt figure, totaling 18 MW between them. OCB1 is the larger of those two, holding 9 of the 18 published megawatts, which makes it the top-ranked campus in the state by that narrow measure. That rank reflects the thinness of published data in Iowa as much as the size of this site. Nine megawatts is a modest footprint by the standards of purpose-built AI campuses being announced elsewhere in the country, and the grid headroom, land availability, or expansion plans for this site are not published.
